newsitem.title: GERMANY: DTB Bunds seen held back in strive for new peak.
newsitem.headline: DTB Bunds seen held back in strive for new peak.

text.p: German Bunds and futures started Wednesday's session in positive territory but analysts said the market was unlikely to venture far this session.
A lack of external trading impetus and a litle wariness in the market would cap gains for the time being, but the broad uptrend which has been in place since early June will also remain intact.

"Tuesday's action really did not provide any new information about the market -- it merely confirmed that while the market is overbought,it still has a bullish undertone," analysts at DMG Futures and Options said in a research note.

They said that while bullish sentiment remained in place, market bears seemed to have all but given up trying to short the market for the time being. "This would actually be suportive very short term, but would also represent a potential sign of caution for the bulls," they said.
By 0636 GMT, the DTB September Bund futures contract was trading four basis points higher on the day at 102.77, having blipped up to 102.79 just after the open.
Analysts said 102.79 represented initial upside resistance for the market, beyond which the contract high at 102.92 would have to be hurdled before the market could push on to 103.00.
With 102.92 now the top of the market's reach in the past two sessions, that barrier is more than likely to prove too tough to overcome this session.
But support is close at hand, with the first aid set to come in around 102.59, just above the day's low on Tuesday.
In the cash market, volumes was likely to remain thin as it has in the past few sessions, analysts said.

"The futures are leading most of the action in the German market at the moment," said one London-based trader. "In the cash we're seeing some curve flattening but there isn't much movement there really."
The 10-year benchmark Bund was quoted at 103.33 by 0651 GMT, offering a bid yield of 5.55 percent.

In terms of relative performance, the German market snatched back its lead from U.S. Treasuries in early European business, pushing the 10-year yield gap out to 82 basis points from around 80 at the end of the European day on Tuesday.
